title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 297
paragraphs: Besides these things, the Egyptians have found out also to what god each month and each day belongs, and what fortunes a man will meet with who is born on any particular day, and how he will die, and what kind of man he will be; and these inventions were taken up by those of the Hellenes who occupied themselves with poetry. Portents too have been found out by them more than by all other men besides; for when a portent has occurred, they observe and write down the event that comes of it, and if ever afterwards something resembling this happens, they believe the event that follows will be similar.
